title: Isaiah Chapter 57 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 57 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 57 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 57.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:1, what happens to the righteous?
options: They perish and no man layeth it to heart
questions.correctAnswer: They perish and no man layeth it to heart
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:1 states that the righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:2 says that the righteous shall enter into peace and rest in their beds.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:2 says, 'He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.'

questions.question: Who does Isaiah 57:3 call 'sons of the sorceress'?
options: The seed of the adulterer and the whore
questions.correctAnswer: The seed of the adulterer and the whore
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:3 addresses the 'sons of the sorceress' as 'the seed of the adulterer and the whore.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:4 accuses people of being children of transgression and a seed of falsehood.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:4 asks, 'are ye not children of transgression, a seed of falsehood,' confirming this accusation.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:5, where do the people enflame themselves with idols?
questions.correctAnswer: Under every green tree
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:5 says, 'Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 57:6, what is described as the portion and lot of the people?
options: Among the smooth stones of the stream
questions.correctAnswer: Among the smooth stones of the stream
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:6 states, 'Among the smooth stones of the stream is thy portion; they, they are thy lot.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:7 says that the people set their bed on a lofty and high mountain to offer sacrifice.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:7 says, 'Upon a lofty and high mountain hast thou set thy bed: even thither wentest thou up to offer sacrifice.'

questions.question: What do the people do behind doors and posts according to Isaiah 57:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Set up their remembrance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:8 says, 'Behind the doors also and the posts hast thou set up thy remembrance.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:9, to whom did the people send messengers far off?
questions.correctAnswer: The king
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:9 says, 'And thou wentest to the king with ointment, and didst increase thy perfumes, and didst send thy messengers far off.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:10 says the people found hope and were grieved.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:10 says they did not say 'There is no hope' and were not grieved, as they found the life of their hand.

questions.question: In Isaiah 57:11, what did the people do instead of remembering God?
options: They lied and did not lay it to heart
questions.correctAnswer: They lied and did not lay it to heart
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:11 asks, 'that thou hast lied, and hast not remembered me, nor laid it to thy heart?'

questions.question: What will not profit the people according to Isaiah 57:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Their righteousness and works
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:12 states, 'I will declare thy righteousness, and thy works; for they shall not profit thee.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:13, who shall possess the land and inherit the holy mountain?
options: He that putteth his trust in the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He that putteth his trust in the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:13 says, 'but he that putteth his trust in me shall possess the land, and shall inherit my holy mountain.'

questions.question: What is the first instruction in Isaiah 57:14?
options: Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way
questions.correctAnswer: Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:14 instructs, 'Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way, take up the stumblingblock out of the way of my people.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 57, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way
He that putteth his trust in me shall possess the land
I will declare thy righteousness and thy works
Upon a lofty and high mountain hast thou set thy bed
questions.correctAnswer: Upon a lofty and high mountain hast thou set thy bed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:7 comes before Isaiah 57:12, 13, and 14, making it the earliest instruction among these options.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 57 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 57 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:8, what action did the people take that showed their unfaithfulness to God?
options: They made a covenant with others and loved their bed
They destroyed the altars of God
They gathered to worship at the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They made a covenant with others and loved their bed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:8 explains that the people discovered themselves to another than God, enlarged their bed, and made a covenant with others, showing unfaithfulness. This is supported by verse 9, which shows further debasement.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 57:9 describe about the people's efforts to seek favor?
options: They went to the king with ointment and sent messengers far off
They built altars on high mountains
They sought God through prayer and humility
questions.correctAnswer: They went to the king with ointment and sent messengers far off
questions.explanation: Verse 9 shows the people going to the king with ointment and increasing perfumes, sending messengers far off, symbolizing efforts to seek favor through worldly means rather than God. This continues the theme of unfaithfulness from verse 8.

questions.question: In Isaiah 57:10, what is said about the attitude of those who are wearied in their way?
options: They say there is no hope and are grieved
They do not say there is no hope and are not grieved
They seek God earnestly and find peace
They confess their sins and repent
questions.correctAnswer: They do not say there is no hope and are not grieved
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states that despite being wearied in their way, they do not say 'There is no hope' and are not grieved because they have found life in their own hands, indicating self-reliance rather than repentance.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:11, what is the reason the people have lied and not remembered God?
options: Because God held His peace even of old and they feared Him not
Because they were under divine protection
Because they were obedient to the law
questions.correctAnswer: Because God held His peace even of old and they feared Him not
questions.explanation: Verse 11 explains that the people lied and did not remember God because He had held His peace for a long time, and they did not fear Him, showing their disregard for God's patience and authority.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 57:12 declare about the people's righteousness and works?
options: They will be rewarded by God
questions.correctAnswer: They will not profit them
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that the righteousness and works of the people will not profit them, emphasizing that their outward actions without true faith are useless.

questions.question: What contrast does Isaiah 57:13 make between trusting in one's companies and trusting in God?
options: Trusting in companies brings security, trusting in God brings loss
Trusting in companies is like the wind carrying them away, trusting in God results in possessing the land
Trusting in companies leads to peace, trusting in God leads to conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in companies is like the wind carrying them away, trusting in God results in possessing the land
questions.explanation: Verse 13 contrasts trusting in one's companies, which are carried away by the wind and vanity, with trusting in God who grants possession of the land and inheritance of the holy mountain, highlighting the superiority of faith in God.

questions.question: What is the practical Christian application of Isaiah 57:14 regarding preparation for God's people?
options: Ignore obstacles and trust God will remove them
Prepare the way and remove stumblingblocks for God's people
Build walls to protect the people from the world
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare the way and remove stumblingblocks for God's people
questions.explanation: Verse 14 instructs to cast up and prepare the way, removing stumblingblocks from the path of God's people, teaching believers to actively work toward spiritual readiness and support for one another.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 57:8-9, what does making a covenant with others and going to the king with ointment symbolize in terms of faithfulness?
options: Faithfulness to God and reliance on Him
Unfaithfulness and reliance on worldly powers
A call to repentance and humility
questions.correctAnswer: Unfaithfulness and reliance on worldly powers
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 together depict the people making covenants and seeking favor from a king with ointment and perfumes, symbolizing turning away from God and relying on worldly means, which is unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 57:10-11 explain the attitude of those who are wearied yet do not despair?
options: They acknowledge no hope and grieve deeply
They rely on their own efforts and do not feel grief
They trust God and repent sincerely
They seek help from others and find peace
questions.correctAnswer: They rely on their own efforts and do not feel grief
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 show that those wearied in their way do not say 'There is no hope' and are not grieved because they find life in their own hands and do not fear God, indicating self-reliance rather than true repentance.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 57:12-13 teach about the efficacy of personal righteousness compared to trust in God?
options: Personal righteousness is sufficient for salvation
Works will profit more than trust in God
Righteousness and works will not profit without trust in God, who grants inheritance
Trusting in God leads to loss of possessions
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness and works will not profit without trust in God, who grants inheritance
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 reveal that personal righteousness and works will not profit, and trusting in God is what leads to possession of the land and inheritance of the holy mountain, teaching the necessity of faith over mere works.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:14, what is the purpose of preparing the way and removing stumblingblocks?
options: To make the path easier for God's people
To isolate God's people from others
questions.correctAnswer: To make the path easier for God's people
questions.explanation: Verse 14 commands to prepare the way and take up stumblingblocks out of the way of God's people, teaching that believers should help remove obstacles to spiritual progress for others.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:15 teaches that God dwells only in the high and holy place and does not associate with the humble spirit.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:15 states that God dwells in the high and holy place and also with the contrite and humble spirit to revive them, showing His nearness to the humble.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 57:16, God will be always wroth and contend forever with His creation.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clarifies that God will not contend forever nor always be wroth, indicating His patience and mercy toward the spirit and souls He created.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:17-18 teaches that God is aware of sinful ways but offers healing and restoration to the repentant.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 17-18 show God's wrath against iniquity but also His observation and willingness to heal, lead, and restore comforts to the repentant and their mourners.

questions.question: What is the message of Isaiah 57:19 regarding peace and healing?
options: Peace is only for those near to God
God creates peace and heals both those far and near
Peace is impossible in a sinful world
Healing is reserved for the righteous only
questions.correctAnswer: God creates peace and heals both those far and near
questions.explanation: Verse 19 declares that God creates the fruit of the lips, peace to him that is far off and near, promising healing to all, demonstrating the universality of God's peace and restoration.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 57 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 57.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:15, where does the 'high and lofty One' dwell?
options: In the high and holy place
In the valley of the shadow
On the earth with the humble
questions.correctAnswer: In the high and holy place
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:15 states that the high and lofty One dwells in the high and holy place, indicating God's transcendence and holiness.

questions.question: What attitude towards God does Isaiah 57:15 emphasize as being accompanied by divine revival?
questions.correctAnswer: Contrite and humble spirit
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:15 highlights that God dwells with the contrite and humble spirit to revive their spirit and heart, emphasizing humility before God.

questions.question: In Isaiah 57:16, for how long will God contend or remain angry?
questions.correctAnswer: Not forever
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:16 states that God will not contend forever nor always be wroth, showing divine patience.

questions.question: What is the reason God gives in Isaiah 57:16 for not contending forever?
options: Because the spirit would fail before Him
questions.correctAnswer: Because the spirit would fail before Him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:16 explains God’s mercy because the spirit would fail before Him, indicating human frailty.

questions.question: What caused God’s wrath according to Isaiah 57:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Iniquity of covetousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:17 states that God's wrath was due to the iniquity of covetousness, showing the seriousness of greed in the original audience’s cultural context.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:18, what is God's promise to those He has seen their ways?
options: He will heal and restore comforts
He will bring judgment and exile
questions.correctAnswer: He will heal and restore comforts
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:18 promises healing and restoration of comforts to those God has seen, reflecting God's merciful character.

questions.question: In Isaiah 57:19, what phrase is repeated to emphasize God's message of peace?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace, peace
questions.explanation: The repetition of 'Peace, peace' in Isaiah 57:19 uses Hebrew parallelism to stress the certainty of God’s peace to those near and far.

questions.question: Who does God say there is no peace for, according to Isaiah 57:21?
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:21 explicitly states that God declares there is no peace for the wicked, showing a strong moral distinction.

questions.question: Isaiah 57:20 compares the wicked to what natural phenomenon?
questions.correctAnswer: The troubled sea
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:20 uses the simile of a troubled sea that cannot rest to illustrate the restless and unclean nature of the wicked.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of humility and divine presence seen in Isaiah 57:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 51:17
questions.explanation: Psalm 51:17 speaks of a broken and contrite heart as pleasing to God, paralleling Isaiah 57:15’s theme of God dwelling with the humble.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the message of peace to those 'far off and near' as in Isaiah 57:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 2:17
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:17 declares Christ came to preach peace to those far and near, echoing the Isaiah 57:19 promise of peace to all.

questions.question: The phrase 'I create the fruit of the lips' in Isaiah 57:19 is an example of which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: The phrase is a metaphor expressing that God brings forth words and declarations (fruit of the lips) symbolizing peace and healing.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew significance of the word translated as 'contrite' in Isaiah 57:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Broken in spirit
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'contrite' (נָשְׁבָּר, nashbar) means broken or crushed, signifying deep humility before God as in Isaiah 57:15.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:18 teaches that God will abandon those who mourn and show repentance.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:18 promises healing, leading, and restoration of comforts to those who mourn, showing God’s care rather than abandonment.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 57:21 declares that the wicked will never experience peace.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:21 states God’s declaration that there is no peace for the wicked, emphasizing their separation from divine peace.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 57 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 57 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 57:1, why is the righteous person's death often unnoticed or unconsidered?
options: Because the righteous is taken away from the evil to come
Because the righteous live long lives
questions.correctAnswer: Because the righteous is taken away from the evil to come
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:1 explains that the righteous perish and no one pays attention because they are taken away from coming evil, indicating divine protection through early removal.

questions.question: What promise is made about the state of the righteous after death in Isaiah 57:2?
options: They shall enter into peace and rest in their beds
They shall be forgotten by all
questions.correctAnswer: They shall enter into peace and rest in their beds
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:2 states that the righteous will 'enter into peace' and 'rest in their beds,' highlighting the hope of eternal peace after death.

questions.question: In Isaiah 57:3, who are addressed as 'sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the whore'?
options: Those engaging in idolatry and falsehood
questions.correctAnswer: Those engaging in idolatry and falsehood
questions.explanation: Verse 3 calls out those involved in spiritual unfaithfulness and idolatry, describing them metaphorically as offspring of immoral spiritual lineage.

questions.question: What practice condemned in Isaiah 57:5 illustrates the depth of Israel's idolatry and wickedness?
options: Slaying children in valleys under cliffs
Offering sacrifices only on the temple mount
questions.correctAnswer: Slaying children in valleys under cliffs
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:5 condemns the practice of child sacrifice, a grievous idolatrous act showing Israel's moral corruption.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 57:6 reveal about the idols worshipped by the people?
options: Their portion is among smooth stones by the stream
They are powerful and provide true comfort
They are hidden in the temple
They are made of gold and silver
questions.correctAnswer: Their portion is among smooth stones by the stream
questions.explanation: Verse 6 metaphorically describes idols as receiving drink and meal offerings among smooth stones, emphasizing their lifeless and unworthy nature.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Isaiah 57:15 where He dwells in the high and holy place and with the contrite spirit?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness and mercy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:15 emphasizes God's holiness ('high and lofty') and His mercy in dwelling with the humble and contrite, reviving their spirits.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 57:16 teach about God's long-suffering and compassion towards humanity?
options: God will not contend forever or remain angry always
God is indifferent to human souls
questions.correctAnswer: God will not contend forever or remain angry always
questions.explanation: Verse 16 reveals God's patient and compassionate nature, showing that He does not remain angry perpetually but desires restoration.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 57:18 depict God's response to the repentant sinner?
options: God heals, leads, and restores comforts
questions.correctAnswer: God heals, leads, and restores comforts
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:18 describes God's gracious response to repentance by healing and comforting the sinner and mourners.

questions.question: Which crucial doctrine is taught by combining Isaiah 57:19 and Isaiah 57:21 regarding peace and wickedness?
options: Peace is a fruit of God's creation given to the faithful, but there is no peace for the wicked
All receive peace regardless of their actions
Peace depends on human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: Peace is a fruit of God's creation given to the faithful, but there is no peace for the wicked
questions.explanation: Verses 19 and 21 together teach that God creates peace for those near and far who trust Him, while the wicked experience no peace, affirming the doctrine of divine peace and judgment.

questions.question: What combined teaching about idolatry and trust in God emerges from Isaiah 57:4-6 and Isaiah 57:13?
options: Idolatry leads to vanity and futility, whereas trusting God results in possessing the land and inheriting the holy mountain
Idolatry is encouraged as a path to peace
Trusting human leaders is better than trusting God
Offering sacrifices to idols brings true comfort
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry leads to vanity and futility, whereas trusting God results in possessing the land and inheriting the holy mountain
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 condemn idolatry and its futility, while verse 13 promises blessing for those who trust God, highlighting the contrast between false worship and true faith.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 57:7-9 depict the people's spiritual adultery and covenant-making with false gods?
options: They set their beds on high mountains and made covenants with others besides God
They worship only in the temple of the Lord
They reject all forms of worship
questions.correctAnswer: They set their beds on high mountains and made covenants with others besides God
questions.explanation: These verses describe idolatrous acts as spiritual adultery, including setting altars on high places and making covenants with foreign gods.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated in Isaiah 57:17 concerning God's reaction to covetousness?
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath and hidden judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 57:17 reveals that God was wroth because of covetousness, smote the sinner, and hid Himself, showing His righteous anger and judgment.

questions.question: What is the apologetic answer to sceptics claiming that the wicked find peace in their own ways, based on Isaiah 57:10-11 and Isaiah 57:20-21?
options: Isaiah teaches that the wicked are wearied and find no peace, likened to a troubled sea
Isaiah confirms that the wicked enjoy lasting peace
Isaiah says the wicked are indifferent and unaffected by their sin
Isaiah supports the idea that peace is independent of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah teaches that the wicked are wearied and find no peace, likened to a troubled sea
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 and 20-21 show that despite weariness, the wicked do not find hope or peace; rather, their lives are restless and troubled, refuting the sceptic's claim.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 57:12 teach about human righteousness and works apart from God?
options: They will not profit or save
They are highly valued by God
questions.correctAnswer: They will not profit or save
questions.explanation: Verse 12 declares that human righteousness and works without God do not benefit or deliver the individual, underscoring the doctrine of salvation by grace.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 57:14 contribute to the redemptive narrative in preparation for God's people?
options: By commanding the removal of stumbling blocks to prepare the way for the people
By declaring the destruction of the temple
By forbidding any change in the land
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding the removal of stumbling blocks to prepare the way for the people
questions.explanation: Verse 14 calls for preparing the way by removing obstacles, symbolizing God's redemptive work to restore His people, linking to messianic prophecy and covenant renewal.
